metadata.theme: Staying calm under pressure, working with others, and thinking a problem through
metadata.premise: Wake Cycle. Astronaut Jun Adair wakes early from a sleep pod on the colony ship Meridian Hope. The crew are not answering, and the ship is drifting toward a dangerous dust anomaly.

items.name: Tool pack
items.description: An orange pack with a clicker light, wire and a spare switch. Dex built it.

clues.name: Dust lane
clues.description: The dust comes in waves. A thin, clear lane runs left of the big rock.

passages.title: Early Wake
paragraphs: A soft click woke Jun Adair.
White light filled the sleep pod. Frost lay thin on the glass.
A calm voice spoke. "Good day, Jun. I am Oru. You woke early."
Jun sat up and rubbed a stiff neck. The pod hall was silent.
"Where is the crew?" Jun asked. "No answer," said Oru. "I do not know why."
Jun took a slow breath. A navigator needs a steady head. Think first, then act.

choices.label: Open the supply locker by the pod
Ask Oru to show the ship log

passages.title: The Orange Pack
paragraphs: Jun lifted the latch on the locker. Inside sat a tool pack with an orange strap.
A tag hung from the strap. It said, "Dex, engine room."
Dex must be awake somewhere. He had left this pack behind in a hurry.
Jun clicked it open. Inside were a clicker light, a coil of wire and a spare switch.
Jun slung the pack onto one shoulder. It sat snug against Jun's back.

choices.label: Walk out into the pod hall
Listen at the door before you go

passages.title: A Whistle In The Vents
paragraphs: Jun paused and listened at the door.
A thin whistle moved through the vents. It rose, then fell, like slow breath.
"That is the dust," said Oru. "It is closer than before."
Jun's neck prickled. Time to move, but stay steady.

choices.label: Walk out into the pod hall

passages.title: Oru's Log
paragraphs: Oru lit a white screen on the wall. Lines of dust crawled across it.
"Dust storm," said Oru. "A strange anomaly. It bends the sensors. Maps may not match what is real."
Jun watched the screen. The dust came in waves. Between two waves, a thin gap stayed clear.
"Where is that gap?" asked Jun. "Left of the big rock," said Oru.
Jun made a note. When sensors lie, a clear lane could save the ship.

choices.label: Walk out into the pod hall
Ask Oru about the crew's last call

passages.title: The Last Call
paragraphs: "What was the crew's last call?" Jun asked.
"A short message," said Oru. "Check the engine room. Then static."
Jun's stomach tightened. Someone down there might need help.
The white screen flickered, then went still.

choices.label: Walk out into the pod hall

passages.title: The Pod Hall
paragraphs: Jun walked between long rows of pods. Four hundred sleepers lay inside.
Every pod glowed green. Green meant safe. Jun checked ten pods, then twenty.
A low whisper ran through the walls. The floor gave a small shake.
"Dust is close," said Oru. "The ship needs help."
Two doors stood ahead. One led up to the bridge deck. One led down to the engine room.

choices.label: Climb up to the bridge deck
Go down to the engine room

passages.title: The Bridge Deck
paragraphs: The bridge deck sat at the top of the ship. Captain Ines Holm slept in a pod by the great wheel.
Her pod light glowed amber, not green. Amber meant the pod was stuck.
"Pod steps go in order," said Oru. "First the latch. Then the switch. Last the hatch."
The latch sat at the foot of the pod. The switch glowed by the glass. The hatch was the lid.
Jun stood still and thought. Which step comes first?

choices.label: Press the switch first
Lift the latch first
Open the hatch first

passages.title: Not Yet
paragraphs: The pod gave a sad buzz. Nothing broke. The pod just waited.
"Order matters," said Oru. "Latch, switch, hatch."

choices.label: Try again, in the right order
Ask Oru why the order matters

passages.title: Latch, Switch, Hatch
paragraphs: "Why does order matter?" Jun asked.
"The latch unlocks," said Oru. "The switch wakes the heartbeat. The hatch lets in air."
"Skip a step, and the pod just waits. It will not break."
Jun nodded, ready to try again, slow and sure.

choices.label: Open the pod in the right order

passages.title: Captain Holm
paragraphs: The latch gave a click. The switch glowed green. The hatch slid back with a hiss.
Captain Holm blinked at the white lamps. She rubbed her neck and sat up.
"Jun? Why am I awake?" Jun told her about the silent crew and the dust.
The Captain tapped the comm panel. It stayed dark. She looked at the thin white haze outside and nodded.
"Calls to far decks cannot get through. That is why no one answered."
She pointed to a rack on the wall. A spare tool pack hung there. "Dex built these. Take one if you have no pack yet."

choices.label: Take the spare pack from the rack
Go to the wheel, no pack needed

passages.title: Dust at the Window
paragraphs: A hard shudder ran through the deck. The screens turned to white static.
Dust whispered along the hull like sand on glass.
"Sensors bent," said Oru. "Maps lie."
Dex's voice crackled from the ship's inside speaker. "The leak is patched. Engines are ready!"
Captain Holm gripped the rail. "Jun, you take the wheel. I will watch the screens."
On the big screen, ghost shapes flickered. Between two dust waves ran a thin, clear lane.

choices.label: Study the dust shapes with the Captain
Take the wheel right away

passages.title: The Engine Room
paragraphs: Jun went down the long steps to the engine room. It was warm and loud.
A lamp swung on a hook. A pair of boots stuck out from under a pipe.
A young engineer slid out. His cheek was smudged with grease. "That is Dex," said Oru.
"Jun? You are awake! I called and called. My calls just hit static!"
A pipe by his knee hissed. A white mist leaked from it. "Coolant," said Dex. "I need hands. Can you help?"

choices.label: Hold the lamp so Dex can see
Pass Dex the tools from the bench

passages.title: Lamp Light
paragraphs: Jun held the lamp high. White light fell on the pipe.
"Watch the seam," said Dex. "Tell me when the mist stops."
Jun watched with care. The mist thinned as Dex tightened the old valve wheel.
"Now," said Jun. "It stopped when you turned it left."

choices.label: Ask Dex what is next
Keep the lamp steady and watch for sparks

passages.title: A Spark By The Wire
paragraphs: Jun kept the lamp steady and watched the wire close.
A spark snapped near the switch. "Back up a little," said Dex.
Jun stepped back. The spark faded, and Dex gave a quick nod.
"Good catch," said Dex. "Now, let's see what is next."

choices.label: Ask Dex what is next

passages.title: Right Tool, Right Time
paragraphs: Jun passed Dex a wrench, then a clamp, then a roll of tape.
Dex worked fast but never rushed. He gave a whip of his wrist and the clamp snapped tight.
He spun the small valve wheel. The hiss faded to nothing.
"Tools in order," said Dex. "That is how you catch a leak."

choices.label: Ask Dex what is next
Sort the spare tools while Dex checks the valve

passages.title: Tools In A Row
paragraphs: Jun sorted the spare tools into the pack.
Click. Click. Each tool found its place.
Dex checked the valve once more. "All steady," he said.
"Nice work. Now, let's see what is next."

choices.label: Ask Dex what is next

passages.title: The Leak Is Gone
paragraphs: The pipe stopped hissing. Dex wiped his hands and grinned.
"Thanks, Jun. The engines can steer now. But our sensors are bent."
"Then we use what we can see," said Jun. Dex nodded. "Good thinking."
He opened a bench drawer. "This spare pack has a clicker light. Take it if you have no pack yet."

choices.label: Take the spare pack
Thank Dex, no pack needed

passages.title: The Paper Chart
paragraphs: Dex tapped a paper chart pinned to the wall. Chalk lines wove across it.
"Paper does not lie," he said. "I drew this from the old logs."
Jun followed the lines with a finger. A thin lane ran left of a big rock.
It did not match the bent screens. The chart looked right.

choices.label: Copy the lane onto your hand screen
Trust your memory

passages.title: The Backup Wheel
paragraphs: A hard shudder shook the room. Pipes rattled and the lamp swung.
Dust whispered along the hull.
Over the speaker, Captain Holm's voice joined them. Oru had woken her pod once the power was steady.
Dex pointed to a backup wheel on the wall. "The ship needs a steady hand. That is you."

choices.label: Take the backup wheel yourself
Ask Dex to come up and help at the wheel

passages.title: Two Heads Are Better
paragraphs: "Come with me," said Jun. "Two heads are better than one."
Dex grabbed a spare lamp and a coil of wire. "Lead the way."
They climbed the steps together as the ship rattled around them.
At the top, the dust storm filled the window in a wall of white.

choices.label: Face the storm together

passages.title: The Wall of Dust
paragraphs: Jun held the wheel. The screen above was a storm of white static.
Ahead, a wall of dust rolled in. Beyond it lay the long road home.
Friends were close. Their voices came through Oru's speaker.
"Choose a plan, Jun," said Oru. "Keep calm. Think it through."

choices.label: Steer through the thin lane left of the rock
choices.lockedHint: Find where the dust is thin first. A log or a chart may show it.

choices.label: Work with the crew to shield the sensors
Cut the engines and wait it out

passages.title: The Thin Lane
paragraphs: Jun turned the wheel slowly to the left. The big rock loomed on the right, dark and rough.
Dust whispered on every side. The clear lane glowed faintly.
"Lane found," said Oru. "Sensors still bent."
Jun kept calm. Breath in. Breath out.
Jun knew a clicker light could cut through dust. It lived in a tool pack.

choices.label: Use the clicker light from the tool pack
choices.lockedHint: Find a tool pack: the locker, the Captain's rack or Dex's bench.

choices.label: Steer by eye and hand alone

passages.title: All Hands
paragraphs: Jun called out the plan. "We will shield the sensors together."
Oru ran a line to every screen. Everyone had a job.
Jun kept the wheel steady. The dust whispered and the lamps flickered.
Two ideas came. Dex could climb to the sensor mast and reset it by hand. Or Jun could wake the watch crew to help.

choices.label: Ask Dex to reset the sensor mast
Wake the watch crew to help

passages.title: The Clear Road
paragraphs: Jun pressed the clicker. A white beam cut through the dust. The sensors blinked awake.
The screens cleared. The big rock slid by on the right. The ship glided down the thin lane.
"Clear road," said Oru. "Good work."
Captain Holm and Dex cheered over the speaker. Dex gave a long, happy whistle.
When the dust fell behind, Jun leaned back and watched the stars. Four hundred sleepers dreamed on, ten years from home.

passages.title: Steady Hands
paragraphs: Jun steered by eye. The dust turned the screens white, but Jun kept the wheel smooth.
The ship scraped the edge of the dust with a rattle. Then it rolled out into clear space.
Some sensors stayed bent. Dex would need a day to fix them. He would not mind.
Jun let out a long breath. A steady head and steady hands were enough, this time.
Next time, Jun thought, a clear plan and the right tools would help even more.

passages.title: The Sensor Mast
paragraphs: Dex clipped his safety line to the rail and climbed the sensor mast. Jun held the wheel and watched the screen.
At the top, Dex found a bent arm. He pushed it back with a click.
The sensors woke. The screens shifted from white to clear. The big rock showed on the right, dark and rough. The clear lane ran to its left.
"Now I see the lane," said Jun. "It is left of the rock!"
They sailed through together. Dex slid down the ladder, rubbing his neck and laughing.
Whatever the dust did next, they would face it as a team.

passages.title: Many Hands
paragraphs: Jun woke the watch crew. Twelve sleepy people shuffled onto the deck.
They split into teams. Some wiped the sensor lenses. Some watched the screens. Some held the lamps.
The ship crept through the dust and out the other side.
It was safe, but the watch crew had lost a few weeks of sleep. They stretched their backs and yawned.
"Worth it," said Captain Holm. Jun nodded. Asking for help had worked, even if it cost something.

passages.title: Drifting Quiet
paragraphs: Jun cut the engines. The ship went quiet. The dust washed over the hull in a long white sigh.
No one was hurt. But the dust pushed the ship far off course, back toward the dark.
"Safe," said Oru. "Late. Try a new plan."
Jun looked at the quiet screens and the empty dark. Maybe a different plan would work.
The stars were still out there. Jun would wake again and try another way.

navigator.definition: A person who plans and checks the way a ship travels.

anomaly.definition: Something strange that does not follow the usual rules.

engineer.definition: A person who builds and fixes machines.

sensors.definition: Tools that let a ship feel and see what is around it.

coolant.definition: A cold liquid that stops engines from getting too hot.

captain.definition: The leader of a ship and its crew.

sleepers.definition: People resting in pods for the long trip.

engines.definition: Machines that push the ship forward.
